claim: A per-option System One scorer in the browser costs 27 MiB of runtime before any weights, and 26-290 MiB of weights after. Every figure is the response body size the browser actually recorded, not a number off a model card.
method: Headless Chromium 141 (Playwright), transformers.js 4.3.0 over ONNX Runtime Web 1.31.0-dev, every Hub file served through a local recording proxy so each byte is counted once. Sizes are uncompressed response bodies in MiB (1,048,576 bytes). The two rlcd-modernbert-151m rows are exact file sizes in bytes from the Hub, converted.
note: The runtime rows are paid once per origin and then cached; the weight rows are paid once per model. ONNX Runtime picks the asyncify WASM build here — the WebGPU (jsep) build is larger still at 27.04 MiB. Nothing in this table is compressed; a CDN will serve the WASM and JS with Brotli, but the .onnx weights are already-compressed tensor data and barely move.
